items.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015
items.q: within a year I was recommended to a tour with Gerry Mulligan. I met a whole bunch of people there.

ctx.x: That’s cool. So the studio work that you did, including the pit band, that’s mostly like word of mouth? You get into New York and you start subbing and do a good job hopefully and then —

Yeah. That’s basically — it’s word of —. I was fortunate. When I moved to New York I had done two albums with Woody. They were both Grammy nominated. I was soloing on it but I wrote most of the music. So I came into town and several people knew who I was, which helped me get past a couple of those early painful stages a lot of people moving to a town fresh out of nowhere have to deal with. So I was subbing on shows within a month of being in New York, and that got me in with the right group of people and I had…
It’s interesting you said that because I wrote down this question I wanted to ask you: what don’t jazz students learn in school?
